GSPip

GSPip is an R package for genomic selection analyses. It integrates: (i) genotype import and quality control, (ii) construction of genomic relationship matrices (GRMs), (iii) optimisation of training populations, and (iv) genomic best linear unbiased prediction (GBLUP) with or without genotype-by-environment (G × E) effects.

Numeric dosage tables, HapMap files, and Variant Call Format (VCF) files are supported. Genomic prediction can be fitted with ASReml-R by residual maximum likelihood (REML) or with Bayesian Generalized Linear Regression (BGLR) by Bayesian reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) regression.

Main functions

Function Purpose Principal result
build_grm() Import genotypes, apply sample and marker quality control, impute missing calls, and construct an additive or dominance GRM gspip_grm object and auditable GRM output files
optimize_training_population() Select a fixed-size training population with Selection of Training Populations by Genetic Algorithm (STPGA) gspip_training_optimization object, selected IDs, convergence records, and random benchmarks
run_gblup_single() Evaluate one stage-1 best linear unbiased estimate (BLUE) per genotype by repeated cross-validation or a fixed split gspip_gblup_single object, metrics, and genotype predictions
run_gblup_gxe() Evaluate stage-1 BLUEs across environments under CV1, CV2, or a fixed genotype-level split gspip_gblup_gxe object, metrics, genotype predictions, and environment-specific predictions
gspip_script() Locate or copy an editable workflow template Path to the installed or copied template

The complete workflow tutorial provides step-by-step analyses for every supported use case.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("FAkohoue/GSPip")

Load the package:

library(GSPip)

The core installation imports AGHmatrix, ASRgenomics, cluster, and data.table. Additional packages are required for specific analyses:

Package or software Use
STPGA Training-population optimisation
rrBLUP Expectation-maximisation genotype imputation
BGLR Open-source Bayesian genomic prediction
ASReml-R Licensed REML genomic prediction
Java and Beagle Linkage-disequilibrium-aware genotype imputation

Install the optional R packages required for STPGA, expectation-maximisation imputation, and BGLR:

install.packages(c("STPGA", "rrBLUP", "BGLR"))

ASReml-R requires a separate installation and a valid licence. Beagle requires Java and a local Beagle JAR file.

Genotype input

build_grm() accepts three genotype formats.

Format Required structure Internal dosage
Numeric table Markers in rows, a marker-ID column, and at least two genotype columns 0, 1, 2, or missing
HapMap Eleven standard HapMap columns through QCcode, followed by sample columns Count of the second allele in alleles
VCF or VCF.GZ Nine fixed VCF columns through FORMAT, followed by sample columns with diploid GT 0/0 = 0, heterozygote = 1, and 1/1 = 2

With input_format = "auto", the extensions .vcf, .vcf.gz, .hmp, .hmp.txt, .hapmap, and .hapmap.txt are detected automatically. Other extensions are treated as numeric input.

Only diploid biallelic markers are converted to dosage. Unsupported records can be removed or rejected with multiallelic_action = "remove" or multiallelic_action = "error". VCF records without an ID receive the identifier CHROM:POS:REF:ALT.

Numeric dosage table 

SNP       CHR  POS    REF  ALT  G001  G002  G003
S1_10234  1    10234  T    G    0     2     2
S1_18945  1    18945  G    T    0     0     0
S1_27656  1    27656  C    T    0     NA    2

Every column not assigned to marker identification, coordinates, alleles, metadata, or marker weights is interpreted as a genotype. Marker IDs and genotype names must be unique.

Marker weights

Marker weights may be supplied as: (i) an inline column in numeric input or (ii) an external table for any supported genotype format.

MarkerID  Weight
S1_10234  1.25
S1_18945  0.80

Weights must be finite and non-negative. At least one retained weight must be positive. Marker weights are supported for the additive VanRaden GRM, but not for the dominance Su GRM.

Quality control and imputation

Sample filtering precedes marker filtering. Marker call rate, minor allele frequency, heterozygosity, and polymorphism are calculated from observed calls before imputation.

imputation_method Method
"none" Retain missing calls and pass them to AGHmatrix::Gmatrix()
"wright" Random imputation from marker allele frequency and genotype-specific Wright inbreeding estimates
"random_hwe" Random imputation from Hardy-Weinberg genotype frequencies
"rrblup_em" Multivariate expectation-maximisation imputation with rrBLUP::A.mat()
"beagle" External Beagle imputation using chromosome, position, reference allele, and alternative allele

Phenotype input

One BLUE per genotype

run_gblup_single() requires one row per genotype.

GenoID  Trait  Population  SE     Weight
G001    10.66  P1          0.566  3.122
G002    10.92  P1          0.385  6.747
G003    10.38  P2          0.457  NA
G004    NA     P2          NA     NA

One BLUE per genotype and environment

run_gblup_gxe() requires one row per genotype × environment combination.

GenoID  Env  Trait  Population  SE     Weight
G001    E1   10.02  P1          0.400  6.250
G001    E2   11.68  P1          0.459  4.747
G002    E1   11.01  P1          0.448  4.982
G002    E2   NA     P1          NA     NA

For an observed BLUE, a positive finite value in Weight is used first. Otherwise, a positive finite standard error (SE) is converted to 1 / SE^2. Rows with a missing trait remain available for prediction and require neither value.

When both precision columns are absent, GSPip uses equal weights, estimates the residual scale, and excludes non-marker effects. Therefore, stage-1 precision information should be supplied when available.

Every phenotype genotype must occur in the GRM. Genotypes present only in the GRM receive missing values in prediction tables unless they are included through a fixed target file.

Genomic relationship matrix and ID files

Optimisation and GBLUP functions require a square, symmetric GRM stored as a comma-separated value (CSV) file. The first column contains genotype IDs; the remaining column names contain the same IDs.

GenoID  G001   G002   G003
G001    1.85  -0.34  -0.21
G002   -0.34   1.91  -0.28
G003   -0.21  -0.28   1.76

Candidate, training, and target files contain one unique ID per row in the column specified by id_col.

GenoID
G001
G002
G003

All listed IDs must occur in the GRM. Candidate and target sets must be disjoint. Fixed training and target sets must also be disjoint.

Quick example

GSPip contains aligned example files with 120 genotypes, 240 markers, three populations, and three environments.

Locate the numeric genotype file and create an output directory:

library(GSPip)

geno_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example_genotypes_numeric.csv",
  package = "GSPip"
)

output_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "gspip-example")
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

Construct an additive VanRaden GRM:

grm_fit <- build_grm(
  geno_file = geno_file,
  output_dir = output_dir,
  input_format = "numeric",
  run_label = "example_grm",
  grm_method = "VanRaden",
  qc_call_rate = 0.95,
  qc_maf = 0.05,
  imputation_method = "wright",
  qc_seed = 123
)

grm_fit
grm_fit$output_files

The returned object contains the GRM, retained marker matrix, marker map, quality-control tables, optional clusters, and paths to all written files.

Training-population optimisation

optimize_training_population() uses GRM principal components as genomic predictors. Trait values are not used during selection.

Two optimisation designs are available:

Mode Objective population
"targeted" A supplied set of target genotypes
"no_test" The complement of each proposed training set within the candidate population

The available STPGA criteria are PEVMEAN, PEVMEAN2, PEVMAX, CDMEAN, CDMEAN2, and CDMAX. All are minimised. Replicated genetic-algorithm searches are reported with equal-size random benchmarks.

Genomic prediction engines

Both GBLUP functions require an explicit engine.

Engine Model fitting Supported random terms
engine = "asreml" REML with ASReml-R Genomic effects and optional non-marker effects
engine = "bglr" Bayesian RKHS regression with BGLR Genomic main effect and, for G × E, a genomic interaction kernel

BGLR estimates the residual scale and requires:

fix_stage1_error  <- FALSE
nonmarker_effects <- FALSE

Its posterior quantities use the suffix _posterior. They are not REML or Cullis estimates. The Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) controls are bglr_n_iter, bglr_burn_in, bglr_thin, and bglr_seed.

Evaluation designs

Analysis Fold unit Prediction target
Single-record cross-validation Genotype One held-out genotype per fold assignment
G × E CV1 Genotype Untested genotypes in all environments
G × E CV2 Genotype × environment record Tested genotypes in environments where their record is held out
Fixed split Genotype A predefined target population

Folds may be balanced with: (i) a supplied population or stratum column, (ii) genomic strata derived from GRM principal components, or (iii) no genotype stratification.

Fixed-split G × E analysis uses CV1 because training and target membership is defined at genotype level.

Output files

Every analysis writes files with the prefix <run_label>_. Existing outputs are preserved unless overwrite_outputs = TRUE.

GRM construction

Suffix Content
_grm.csv Genomic relationship matrix
_sample_qc.csv Sample missingness and filter status
_marker_qc.csv Marker statistics and filter status
_marker_map.csv Retained marker coordinates and alleles
_qc_report.txt Quality-control counts and thresholds
_grm_info.txt Matrix diagnostics and inversion result
_clusters.csv Optional GRM principal components and cluster assignments
_imputed_genotypes.csv Optional final marker matrix

Training-population optimisation

Suffix Content
_selected_training.csv Selected training genotypes
_target_ids.csv Target genotypes for fixed-split prediction
_ga_replicates.csv Objective value and seed for every genetic-algorithm replicate
_ga_convergence.csv Objective trajectory for every replicate
_random_benchmark.csv Objectives for equal-size random training sets
_pc_variance.csv GRM eigenvalues and principal components used

GBLUP evaluation

Suffix Content
_metrics.csv Fold- and iteration-level statistics
_summary.csv Mean and standard deviation across iterations
_cv_predictions.csv Out-of-sample genotype predictions
_cv_predictions_by_env.csv G × E predictions by genotype and environment
_train_predictions.csv In-sample genomic predictions
_train_se.csv ASReml standard errors or BGLR posterior standard deviations
_split_ids.csv Training and target membership for a fixed split
_derived_strata*.csv Optional genomic-strata assignments and diagnostics
_run_info.txt Analysis settings and package versions

The principal performance statistics are prediction ability, accuracy, root mean squared error (RMSE), standardised RMSE, proportion of variance explained (PVE), and heritability. Environment-specific and stratum-specific statistics are added when their corresponding analyses are requested.

Example data

The complete example set is available as R objects:

data(gs_example_all)
names(gs_example_all)
dim(gs_example_all$geno)  # 120 × 240
dim(gs_example_all$grm)   # 120 × 120

Equivalent numeric, HapMap, and VCF genotype files are installed under extdata. The same directory contains the GRM, single-record BLUEs, G × E BLUEs, marker weights, candidate IDs, and target IDs used in the vignette.

Editable workflow templates

The exported functions form the package application programming interface (API). Editable templates are also available for analyses organised through settings files:

gspip_script("grm_builder", copy_to = "analysis/")
gspip_script("optimize_training_population", copy_to = "analysis/")
gspip_script("gblup_cv_single", copy_to = "analysis/")
gspip_script("gblup_cv_gxe", copy_to = "analysis/")

Each template is a thin wrapper around the corresponding exported function. Therefore, direct function calls and template-based analyses use the same implementation.
